newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end down as specs begin to liquidate.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end down as specs begin to liquidate.

text.p: FCOJ futures settled weaker on mostly speculative liquidation, market sources said.
Trade buying in the March/May and the March/July spreads held prices at the lows in hefty volume estimated at 5,000 lots. Thursday's official volume was 4,716 lots.
Most-active May ended 1.95 cents lower at 81.85 cents a lb, traded 83.90 to 81.55. Spot March closed down 2.10 at 79.05.
Analysts said prices could remain in a trading range through the March delivery period. The last trading day for the spot month is March 10.
Firm support in May was seen at the recent low of 77.50.

Longer-term, prices could fall as juice inventories swell. The Florida Citrus Processors Association on Thursday put frozen concentrated orange juice movement at only 5.594 million gallons for the week ended February 15.

"The crop is bigger, inventories are larger and we need to move a lot more juice than in the past," an analyst said, noting that a weekly movement of 4.0 million gallons was considered strong in past years.
"Demand is not there because retail prices are high and until we lower prices we won't drain the huge inventories." she said.
